meta.name: Reprice tour packages dynamically with Claude, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Dynamic Tour Package Repricing Engine

Airline-style yield management for tour packages. This workflow continuously pulls live booking/demand signals and competitor pricing, scores each package's demand momentum and seasonality, checks price positioning against the market, and lets AI finalize a margin-protecting price - live, without a revenue manager repricing by hand.

### Who's it for
- Tour operators and OTAs running multiple departures per package across a season
- Revenue management teams that want airline-style dynamic pricing without building it from scratch
- Anyone whose current process is a person periodically eyeballing a spreadsheet of bookings and competitor prices

### How it works
1. A schedule trigger polls a live booking/demand API and a competitor pricing API for every active package
2. JS - Calculate Demand Score, Seasonality & Competitor Position scores each package's booking velocity and occupancy, applies a seasonality/urgency curve based on days-to-departure, and compares list price against competitor average to compute a total recommended price adjustment
3. Packages whose recommended adjustment is 3% or more are filtered through for repricing
4. AI finalizes the price - applying sane rounding and a sanity cap - and writes a short reasoning note with a confidence level
5. The new price and reasoning are appended to a PriceUpdates log for downstream systems and audit
6. The revenue management team gets a Slack alert summarizing what changed and why

### How to set up
1. Import this workflow into n8n
2. Add Anthropic Claude credentials and attach to the Anthropic model node
3. Point Fetch Live Demand & Booking Data at your real booking system/API and add its auth header
4. Point Fetch Competitor Pricing Data at your real competitor-pricing feed/API and add its auth header
5. Switch the Google Sheets HTTP node to the native Google Sheets node with OAuth2, or add OAuth2 credentials directly
6. Replace YOUR_SHEET_ID with your actual Spreadsheet ID
7. Add Slack credentials and replace YOUR_SLACK_CHANNEL_ID
8. Set the schedule interval to match how often demand/competitor data should be checked (default: every 30 minutes)
9. Activate the workflow

### Requirements
- Anthropic Claude API key (claude-sonnet-4 recommended)
- A booking/demand data API and a competitor pricing API
- Google Sheets with OAuth2 credentials (PriceUpdates tab)
- Slack workspace access for the revenue management alert

### How to customize
- Adjust the seasonality curve and competitor-adjustment thresholds in JS - Calculate Demand Score, Seasonality & Competitor Position
- Change the 3% needsReprice threshold to reprice more or less frequently
- Add a maximum single-run price-change cap so no departure jumps too far in one cycle
- Add per-cabin/per-room-type tiers if your packages have multiple sellable fare classes

### Google Sheets Column Layout

PriceUpdates tab - row 1 headers:
Repriced At | Package ID | Package Name | Base Price USD | Final Price USD | Price Change % | Demand Score | Seasonality Adj % | Competitor Adj % | Confidence | Reasoning

## Stage 1: Demand, Seasonality & Competitor Scoring

Schedule Trigger polls on a fixed interval (default every 30 minutes). Two API calls run in parallel: Fetch Live Demand & Booking Data (API 1) pulls booking velocity, occupancy, and capacity per package; Fetch Competitor Pricing Data (API 2) pulls the current market average price per package.

Merge - Combine Demand & Competitor Data joins both datasets into a single item by position.

JS - Calculate Demand Score, Seasonality & Competitor Position (Code Node 1) computes days-to-departure and occupancy, a 0-100 demandScore from booking velocity, a seasonality/urgency adjustment based on how close departure is, and a competitor adjustment based on how far list price sits from the market average - combining all three into a single recommended price and a needsReprice flag.

Split Out - Packages turns that single array into one item per package so the rest of the workflow can evaluate each package independently.

## Stage 2: AI Yield Repricing Decision

Filter - Packages Needing Reprice lets through only packages whose combined demand/seasonality/competitor adjustment is 3% or more, so stable packages are never touched.

Wait - API Rate Limit (Wait Node 1) respects API rate limits, then the yield-management AI (claude-sonnet-4, temperature 0.2 for consistent, conservative pricing) finalizes the price - applying sensible rounding and a sanity cap - and writes a one-line reasoning note plus a confidence level.

JS - Parse AI Repricing Output (Code Node 2) extracts the structured JSON safely, with a fallback that uses the raw calculated recommendation if AI parsing fails.

Wait - Sheets Write Rate Limit (Wait Node 2) paces the write-back before it hits Google Sheets.

## Stage 3: Price Log & Alert

JS - Format Repricing Update & Log Row (Code Node 3) builds the audit row: base price, final price, price change %, and the demand/seasonality/competitor factors that drove the decision.

Log New Price to Google Sheets PriceUpdates appends that row - the living source of truth downstream systems can read to sync the live price.

Send Slack Alert to Revenue Management Team posts a short summary so the revenue team has visibility into every autonomous price change as it happens.

parameters.text:
=You are a revenue management analyst applying airline-style yield management to tour packages.

Package: {{ $json.packageName }} ({{ $json.packageId }})
Departure: {{ $json.departureDate }} ({{ $json.daysToDeparture }} days out)
Occupancy: {{ $json.occupancyRate }}% ({{ $json.capacityRemaining }} of {{ $json.totalCapacity }} seats remaining)
Booking Velocity: {{ $json.bookingsLast7Days }} bookings in last 7 days
Demand Score: {{ $json.demandScore }}/100
Seasonality/Urgency Adjustment: {{ $json.seasonalityFactor }}%
Competitor Avg Price: {{ $json.competitorAvgPriceUSD }} USD (we are {{ $json.competitorPriceIndex }}% vs market)
Competitor Adjustment: {{ $json.competitorAdjustmentPct }}%
Current Base Price: {{ $json.basePriceUSD }} USD
Target Margin: {{ $json.targetMarginPct }}%
Calculated Total Adjustment: {{ $json.totalAdjustmentPct }}% -> Recommended Price: {{ $json.recommendedPriceUSD }} USD

Finalize the price. Apply sensible psychological rounding (e.g. end in .00 or .99) and never move price more than 15% from the current base price in a single cycle, even if the calculated adjustment suggests more. Write one short sentence explaining the decision and a confidence level.

Return a JSON object with EXACTLY these fields:
{
  "finalPriceUSD": number,
  "priceChangePct": number,
  "reasoning": "One short sentence for internal audit",
  "confidence": "High, Medium, or Low"
}

Return ONLY the JSON. No markdown, no explanation.
